appraisal_events.evidence: "Laissez-moi donc tranquille avec vos maîtres, vous en savez dix fois autant que lui... Vous ne tuez pas vos malades, vous au moins!" followed by Cottard's ironic invocation of Potain and Mme Verdurin's laughing admission "vous me faisiez monter à l'arbre."
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin explicitly elevates Cottard's competence over the official medical establishment, though the narrator frames her self-dramatizing bravado ironically and she ends the exchange laughingly admitting Cottard's irony had drawn her in.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. Verdurin "se contenta de tirer une bouffée de sa pipe en songeant avec tristesse qu'il ne pouvait plus rattraper sa femme sur le terrain de l'amabilité."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly compares the couple and shows M. Verdurin conceding that he can no longer match his wife's charm and wit, a local comparative diminishment of him relative to her.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Vous savez que votre ami nous plaît beaucoup... Il est simple, charmant; si vous n'avez jamais à nous présenter que des amis comme cela, vous pouvez les amener."
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin praises Swann unreservedly to Odette and explicitly invites him to be brought back, marking his welcome entry into the Verdurin circle.

status_effects.explanation: Cottard is locally praised by Mme Verdurin as far more competent than the celebrated "maîtres" of the profession.
He privately concedes he can no longer keep pace with his wife's charm, a quiet yielding of ground within the couple.
The same comparison that diminishes her husband confirms her as the one with the upper hand in charm and "amabilité."
Mme Verdurin's unhedged praise ("simple, charmant," "nous plaît beaucoup") clearly elevates Swann in this local verdict.
Mme Verdurin explicitly opens the boundary of her circle to Swann, inviting Odette to bring him again, a clear crossing into the Verdurin salon's valued inner space.

ambiguities: The closing remark names Swann only as "votre ami" and is addressed to Odette; the identification with Swann relies on his presence and engagement in the immediately preceding context rather than on any name given within the passage itself.

Mme Verdurin's exchange with Cottard is layered with narrator irony (her self-dramatizing 'courage de ses opinions' and her own admission of being teased, 'vous me faisiez monter à l'arbre'); this uncertainty is reflected in E1's ironized stance, and no separate status effect is assigned to Mme Verdurin from this exchange given the unclear balance between comic exposure and continued command of the room.
